title: Grateful Dead Live at Manor Downs on 1982-07-31
lineage: SBD > Cassette Master > DAT (44.1khz) > Sony R500 > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude Professional v7.02 > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Tight, high‑energy 1982 Manor Downs show captured on a solid soundboard mix, featuring standout performances of Candyman, Scarlet Begonias → Fire On The Mountain and a smoking Morning Dew.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this July‑31‑1982 set as one of the era’s finest – the band is tight yet loose, delivering fire‑filled renditions from Candyman through Deal and a marathon second half highlighted by Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain, Uncle John’s Band → Truckin’ and an epic Morning Dew.  The Charlie Miller soundboard recording is praised as clear, well‑balanced and “A” quality despite some heat‑induced static early in the show.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance (tight playing, high energy, many standout songs) and recording (clear, well‑mixed soundboard), with only minor technical glitches noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and balanced; praised as "very good" and "primo" mix. Some heat‑related PA issues early in the set, static on Uncle John’s Band, and a monitor blow that caused brief distortion, but overall listenable.

standout_songs: Scarlet Begonias → Fire On The Mountain
poor_songs: Uncle John's Band (monitor blow and static)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth transitions with notable segues (Estimated>Eyes, UJB into Truckin'). The first set builds solidly; the second set maintains momentum and ends on a high‑energy Morning Dew.

band_member_comments.Jerry: In top form all night – crisp guitar tone, strong solos, birthday energy; minor lyric flubs but overall stellar.
band_member_comments.Bob: Possibly added a spontaneous Happy Birthday shout during the show (per an attendee).
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent contributed solid keyboard work and shared vocals on Candyman; overall keyboards praised as well‑balanced in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart were described as “an extra step above” their usual standard, sounding like one drummer with eight arms.
